evidence.note: Benchmarks the full 10 timed shapes and identifies worst offenders (N=2048 ~95ms, N=1024 D=384 over target), establishing a latency worst-case view early.
Reports precise per-shape medians against the 10400μs gate (N=2048 ~35.6ms, N=1024 D=384 ~10.7ms over), pinpointing which shapes fail.

Explicitly anticipates one-helps-one-hurts ('if it helps D=384 but hurts N=2048, dispatch can be adjusted'), and tracks that several shapes improved while N=2048 stays ~25.9ms above target — clear binding-shape awareness plus cross-case regression catching.

Catches that einsum, fused-final, and max-autotune experiments regress specific shapes or break correctness (maxdiff ~0.105) and reverts each; correctness checks are only small D=128/D=384 masked/nomask smoke tests, not a grid ledger, and no Cauchy-specific correctness tracking.
Submits while N=2048 remains ~2.5x over budget after repeatedly cycling variants on the same shape, without recognizing the circular thrash or that the gate is unmet — no stuck-state detection.

reasoning: On the latency axis the agent shows level-8 behavior: per-shape medians against the 10400μs gate, consistent identification of N=2048,D=128 as the binding worst-case, and reliable catching of cross-case regressions (steps 8, 12-14, 16-20). But correctness monitoring is coarse — only small smoke tests, no explicit grid ledger and no distinct Cauchy tracking (level-5 quality) — and it never detects its own circular re-tuning of the bottleneck shape, submitting still far over budget (steps 21-22). Averaging strong latency awareness with weaker correctness ledger and absent stuck-state detection lands it at 6.
